sourceTitle: Goodman service manual RS6621003r3 (June 2020), 80% single-stage gas furnaces GMES80, AMES80, GCES80, ACES80, VMES80 and VCES80, troubleshooting chart
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
displayPattern: Diagnostic LED through the blower-door window on an 80% single-stage *MES80 or *CES80 furnace: Goodman GMES80 and GCES80, Amana AMES80 and ACES80, GMC VMES80 and VCES80. Count the flashes between pauses. This is not the 7-segment EE display on a 90%+ furnace.
meaning: Rollout limit is open, or the integrated control module fuse is blown. The furnace does not heat.
causes: Misaligned burners, a blocked flue and/or air inlet, or a failed induced draft blower
The abnormal-operation section also names restricted flue piping or improper combustion air, and says the circulator runs all the time when the rollout control is open
A short in the 24 volt control or safety circuits
diySteps: Turn the furnace off. Do not reset a rollout switch
Look at the outdoor vent termination for a blockage you can see without taking the vent apart
Technician: the chart's checks are burner alignment, flue and inlet piping, the rollout limit, inducer performance, wiring, and the control-module fuse
proAdvice: Six flashes can be rollout or a blown fuse. Rollout means flame left the burner area. Leave the furnace off and call a licensed HVAC technician. This chart is service manual RS6621003r3 for those 80% single-stage models. A 7-segment code such as EE0 or EE2 is a different furnace family.
